post.description:
401 for every failure -- wrong password, unknown email, disabled or
locked -- so this cannot be used to find out who has an account. Ten
failures in a row lock the account for fifteen minutes.
Ends the session on the server, not just in this browser.

get.summary: Extraction spend in a date window

post.description:
Upload a file for processing. It belongs to the caller's organisation.

Deduplicated by SHA-256 of the contents, per organisation: uploading the
same bytes twice returns the original document with `duplicate: true` and
queues no extra work. Safe to retry.
Same as `POST /documents`, for callers that already hold the bytes.

get.description: Current status plus the full audit trail of how it got there.

The bytes exactly as uploaded, to view beside what was extracted from them.

Served as the type detected at upload -- never one the caller names -- and
only types on the upload allowlist ever got stored, so nothing here can be
HTML or SVG and run in a browser. `nosniff` stops the browser guessing
otherwise, and `no-store` keeps documents full of personal data out of
every cache on the way.

The recognised text, the engine that produced it, and the confidence.

Returns 404 with distinct messages for "no such document" and "OCR has not
run yet", because those need different actions from the caller.

get.description:
What a client system imports: the extracted fields, normalised, with what
was read, what was worked out, what failed review, and the ledger row.

Answers 200 in every state -- poll until `outcome` is not "processing".
Only an unknown document is a 404.
Liveness: the process is up and the database answers. Nothing more.

post.description:
A draft of a new processor, or of a published version of an existing one
(`based_on_version`). Nothing routes to a draft until it is published.

Describe the document in plain language; a model drafts the processor and
it is saved as a draft for a person to review, try and publish. Never with
a transform: code is written by people. If the draft does not validate
after one repair attempt, nothing is saved and the YAML comes back with
its problems, to fix by hand.
post.summary: Have a model draft a processor

put.description:
Admin only. Takes effect on the next document routed: access belongs to
the processor, not to a version, so nothing needs publishing.

post.description:
409 if another version was published after this draft was started: the
response names it, so the caller can merge from it.
post.summary: Make a draft the live version

post.description:
Billed like any extraction. On a stored document the attempt is recorded
as a trial -- in the cost report, never the document's result.
post.summary: Try a version on a stored document or on text

post.description:
Read like a real document (text layer, else OCR) but not ingested, so the
real copy is not deduplicated away when it arrives. Not recorded.
post.summary: Try a version on an uploaded sample

get.description:
Readiness: the database is at the migration this code expects.

The check `/health` cannot make. An empty or half-migrated database
passes `/health`, and then every real request fails (DESIGN §8.2), so a
load balancer or orchestrator should route traffic on this one. 503 with
the reason until the schema matches.
